title: Intel Honors Two Indian American Professors With Outstanding Researcher Awards for AI Work
excerpt: Purdue's Vijay Raghunathan and Georgia Tech's Visvesh Sathe, both IIT alumni, recognized for contributions to energy-efficient computing and AI hardware innovation.
body:
• Purdue University's Vijay Raghunathan and Georgia Tech's Visvesh Sathe have received Intel's 2025 Outstanding Researcher Awards for their work in AI and semiconductor innovation.
  • Both researchers are graduates of IIT Bombay and have built distinguished careers in energy-efficient computing and AI hardware design at leading American universities.
  • The Intel award recognizes contributions to nanoelectronic and manufacturing technologies with demonstrated industrial relevance.
  • Their research addresses critical challenges in making AI systems more efficient and scalable for real-world deployment.

Intel Corporation has recognized two Indian American professors — Vijay Raghunathan of Purdue University and Visvesh Sathe of the Georgia Institute of Technology — with its 2025 Outstanding Researcher Awards, according to The American Bazaar. The honor highlights their contributions to advancing energy-efficient computing and AI hardware technologies.

Two IIT Alumni Driving American AI Innovation

Raghunathan, a professor of electrical and computer engineering at Purdue, is one of the leading experts in the design of energy-harvesting embedded systems. His research spans hardware and software architectures for embedded systems, wireless sensors for the Internet of Things, and wearable and implantable electronics, with particular emphasis on low-power design.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=FBzd9AozpkQ

An IEEE Fellow and ACM Fellow, Raghunathan also serves as Purdue's vice president for global partnerships and programs and as director of the university's semiconductor education initiatives. He received the NSF CAREER Award and the IEEE/ACM Design Automation Conference Under-40 Innovators Award. He co-directs the SRC/DARPA-funded Center for the Co-design of Cognitive Systems and is the founding co-director of the Purdue-led Center for a Secured Microelectronics Ecosystem.

Sathe, an associate professor of electrical and computer engineering at Georgia Tech, leads the Processing Systems Lab (PSyLab), which focuses on energy-efficient computing, implantable electronics, and run-time hardware optimization for digital and mixed-signal systems. He previously held positions at the University of Washington and in AMD's Low-Power Advanced Development Group, where he invented and translated energy-efficient circuit technologies such as resonant clocking into production microprocessors.

"I'm hoping that to my current and future students, the award will serve as an affirmation of the relevance and potential impact of the research they have painstakingly performed over the years, especially given the high costs and risks associated with integrated circuits research."

— Visvesh Sathe, Georgia Tech

What the Intel Award Recognizes

The Intel Outstanding Researcher Award is presented for outstanding contributions to the development of advanced nanoelectronic and manufacturing technologies. In selecting winners, Intel considers fundamental insights, industrial relevance, technical difficulty, communications, and potential student hiring associated with a candidate's research program. The award was created to recognize contributions by researchers funded through Intel's Semiconductor Technology Council and associated Strategic Research Sectors.

Both Raghunathan and Sathe hold B.Tech. degrees from IIT Bombay. Raghunathan went on to build his career at Purdue, while Sathe completed his M.S. and Ph.D. at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, before joining Georgia Tech. Sathe also serves on the technical program committees of the IEEE Custom Integrated Circuits Conference and the International Solid-State Circuits Conference, and is a distinguished lecturer of the IEEE Solid-State Circuits Society.

Indian Americans Leading Semiconductor Research

The recognition adds to a growing list of Indian American researchers shaping the future of AI and semiconductor technology in the United States. Raghunathan was recently appointed as an inaugural member of the Workforce Advisory Board for the National Semiconductor Technology Center, reflecting the broader role Indian American academics play in guiding U.S. technology policy.

At Purdue, Raghunathan has been instrumental in building the U.S.–India Center of Excellence in Semiconductors with IIT Hyderabad, connecting research and workforce development across both countries. "The United States brings leadership in advanced semiconductor research and innovation, while India brings scale, talent, and bold ambitions in manufacturing," he told SPAN Magazine.

What's Next

Both researchers continue to lead federally funded research centers focused on AI hardware, semiconductor systems, and next-generation computing. Georgia Tech, where Sathe is based, recently joined an $840 million Department of Defense project to develop next-generation semiconductor microsystems. Purdue, meanwhile, has positioned itself as a national leader through partnerships with SK hynix and its Institute of Chips and AI, launched in Silicon Valley in late 2024.
